meta.description: Analyze Perturb-seq / CROP-seq single-cell CRISPR screens. Use when assigning guides as a mixture problem, removing non-perturbed escaper cells with Mixscape, choosing a calibrated test (SCEPTRE conditional resampling) over naive DE, quantifying effect size with E-distance, separating compositional shifts from within-state expression change, or judging whether a perturbation-prediction foundation model actually beats a baseline.

scientific_integrity.detail: All 7 outputs use real data, real installed packages, or real citations. New this round: independently verified via CRAN/Bioconductor/GitHub that sceptre is GitHub-only (Katsevich-Lab/sceptre, R>=4.1 per its own DESCRIPTION) and scMAGeCK was released then removed from Bioconductor at 3.17 (not merely 'unreleased staging' as SKILL.md now states) -- both are real, checkable facts, and neither output fabricates a DOI, p-value, or result.

practice_boundaries.detail: Purely computational/research skill; no diagnostic, prescriptive, or patient-level claims anywhere.

methodological_ground.detail: Core prose guidance remains textbook-correct. The Milo replacement (per-(replicate x target) pseudo-sample, one-target-vs-NT contrast) is methodologically sound and independently confirmed to generalize to a second target (ATF2) beyond the one the fixer verified (STAT1).

code_usability.detail: 6 of 7 inputs now produce real, independently-executed, runnable code (up from 5/7 pre-fix): Mixscape (confirmed via a 4,000-cell subsample of the real dataset -- clean run, no KeyError, no CSC error), SCEPTRE (fully executed end to end after this re-audit independently corrected the sceptre install/R-version documentation and installed it live), E-distance/E-test, and Pseudobulk+Milo (confirmed on 2 targets). scMAGeCK remains code-free by design (honestly reframed, not fabricated) -- N/A, not a failure.

functional_suitability.note: Both flagship worked examples (guide assignment + Mixscape, Milo/pseudobulk) now run correctly as shipped. Residual gap found this round: SKILL.md's SCEPTRE Prerequisites (`install.packages('sceptre')`, 'requires R >= 4.5') is itself factually wrong -- sceptre is not on CRAN or Bioconductor at all (both return 404); it is GitHub-only (Katsevich-Lab/sceptre) and its DESCRIPTION requires R (>= 4.1), confirmed by installing and running it live in this env's real R 4.4.3.

reliability.note: Common Errors table now covers both fixed defects (KeyError, Milo AssertionError) with accurate fixes. Docked because the sceptre guidance actively misdirects: it tells the agent 'R needs upgrading' when the real fix (remotes::install_github) works fine under R 4.4.3 -- a dead end, not a fix.

performance_context.note: New finding this round: `Mixscape.perturbation_signature()` on the real, full 20,729-cell papalexi_2021 dataset shows heavy, undocumented resource cost -- two independent clean-environment attempts grew past 20GB RAM and were terminated to protect the shared machine before completing (the fixer's own report and my subsample-of-4,000-cells run both completed cleanly, so the code is correct, just resource-heavy in a way SKILL.md never flags). E-test compute cost also still unflagged (carried over from pre-fix).

recommendations.title: SCEPTRE install instructions in SKILL.md remain factually wrong
recommendations.problem: SKILL.md's Prerequisites still say `install.packages('sceptre')` and 'requires R >= 4.5'. Neither is correct: sceptre is not distributed on CRAN or Bioconductor at all (both return 404), it is GitHub-only (Katsevich-Lab/sceptre), and its own DESCRIPTION requires R (>= 4.1). This re-audit installed and ran it successfully under this env's real R 4.4.3.
recommendations.root_cause: The original tooling env's TOOLS.md misdiagnosed a 'not on CRAN' failure as 'filtered by R-version gate,' and both the original audit and the fix inherited that claim without checking the package's actual distribution channel.
recommendations.fix: Replace `install.packages('sceptre')` with `remotes::install_github('Katsevich-Lab/sceptre')` and correct the R-version note to R >= 4.1 (per the package's own DESCRIPTION).

recommendations.title: Mixscape's perturbation_signature is undocumented-heavy on the real full-size dataset
recommendations.problem: Two independent, unloaded attempts to run the shipped example verbatim on the full 20,729-cell papalexi_2021 dataset grew past 20GB RAM without completing and were terminated to protect the shared machine. A clean run on a 4,000-cell subsample of the same data completed correctly in under a minute, so the fix is correct -- the cost is real and scales badly with cell count, not the fixer's bug.
recommendations.root_cause: pertpy 1.3.0's Mixscape.perturbation_signature implementation appears to have superlinear memory scaling with cell count for this dataset's neighbor-signature computation; SKILL.md gives no resource guidance at all for this step (only the E-test's runtime is flagged, not Mixscape's memory footprint).
recommendations.fix: Add a note next to the Mixscape section warning that perturbation_signature can require significant memory on datasets of this size (tens of GB observed on ~20k cells) and suggesting a subsample or batched approach for memory-constrained environments.

recommendations.title: scMAGeCK's Bioconductor history is described imprecisely
recommendations.problem: SKILL.md says scMAGeCK is on 'Bioconductor's unreleased staging index' -- it was actually released and then removed from Bioconductor at release 3.17 (confirmed via bioconductor.org/about/removed-packages/), which is a different history than 'never released.'
recommendations.root_cause: The reframing correctly identified scMAGeCK's current unavailability but did not check whether it had ever had a full release.
recommendations.fix: Change 'unreleased staging index' to 'released through Bioconductor 3.16, then removed at 3.17' for accuracy.
